artifacts.summary: Five-phase plan (4.75h) delivering the choice-free state-set route as one new Independence/ leaf module, with absolute pins at the ShiftSet avatar and relative pins at translationFrame.

memory_candidates.content: Choice-hygiene work over this repo's TemporalOrder bundle turns on three measured asymmetries, each discovered the slow way. (1) #print axioms traverses a declaration's TYPE as well as its value, so a choice-borne frame constant makes every theorem ABOUT it choice-borne however the proof is built -- only an absolute pin at a @[reducible] constructor avatar escapes; a pin at the constant can only ever be relative. (2) At a TemporalOrder, add_lt_add_right is [propext] while add_lt_add_left and sub_pos are [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]; abs_eq_zero and exists_ne are likewise choice-borne, replaceable by by_contra+abs_pos.mpr and exists_pair_ne+lt_trichotomy. Write witnesses additively (-(tau.state 0) + v) and never reach for sub_pos. (3) ShiftSet.fibre_isRegular takes the Limit obligation from the structure's own sep field and never calls TaskFrame.limit_of_shift, which is the single Classical.choice source in the frame-construction neighbourhood -- routing a frame through ShiftSet rather than FrameOver.ofReflectiveRegular is what makes a whole chain choice-free. Separately: shrinking a pinned axiom set is a GOOD change that still trips check-module-invariants.sh C2/C14's exact-string baseline (a HARD STOP, not a new baseline), so re-baselining is a user decision, not a task detail.
